title: Research
Research
text:
Papers

Growth Rate of Essential Surfaces via Measured Laminations
Brevan Ellefsen, 2026. arXiv:2608.08833

We show that in any Haken 3-manifold \(M\), the dimensions of \(\ML(M)\) and \(\ML_0(M)\) can be calculated using normal surfaces. As a corollary, we prove the number of closed orientable essential surfaces of Euler characteristic at least \(-2n\) in a closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold with \(H_2(M,\Z/2\Z) = 0\) is asymptotic to \(n^{\dim \ML_0(M)}\).

title: Research
text:
Current Research

Least-Weight Laminations

I am currently working to show all measured laminations admit normal representatives which are “minimal” with respect to combinatorial weight (intersections with the \(1\)-skeleton), with the hope to build a concrete realization of Hatcher’s \(\ML\).



Volume Bounds on Growth

Now that \(\dim \ML\) is known to count surfaces by genus, I am interested in how \(\ML\) varies as one changes the underlying 3-manifold. In particular, I am interested in whether one can bound \(\dim \ML(M)\) in terms of \(\operatorname{vol}(M)\) for a compact, hyperbolic \(M^3\).



Minimal Laminations

Building off results of Freedman, Hass, and Scott in the surface case, and Sullivan in the foliation case, I hope to understand when their work can be bridged to prove certain classes of laminations admit leaves which are all minimal with respect to some ambient metric.

title: Research
text:
Other Interests
I am generally interested in topological and geometric structures on 3-manifolds, including pseudo-Anosov flows and veering triangulations. I am particularly interested in methods that can be made computational.
I am also interested in dynamical problems, particularly those that can be tackled using ergodic and specification techniques.

title: Curriculum Vitae
Brevan Ellefsen
text:
Research
My current research concerns the structure of measured lamination spaces of 3-manifolds and their relationship with normal surface theory. Particular goals of this research are to understand essential surface counts, to define a computable model of \(\ML\) using least-weight laminations, and to understand how these spaces change in relation to hyperbolic volume.
My paper Growth Rate of Essential Surfaces via Measured Laminations is available on the arXiv.
See my research page for more about my work.
See my cv for a complete history of my research.
